key_insight: Real-world sensitivity of an FDA-cleared pulmonary embolism triage AI was 64.1%, versus 93% in its clearance summary, and varied by site and embolus location.
clinical_relevance: Lower detection sensitivity, particularly for peripheral emboli, underscores the importance of local validation and ongoing monitoring of AI triage tools.
method: Retrospective evaluation of 14,736 CT pulmonary angiography examinations across six sites, July 2023–March 2026.
Report-derived reference labels used an LLM pipeline validated against 600 radiologist-annotated reports (κ = 0.98).
Assessed performance across demographic and embolus subgroups, sites, and time.
evidence_signal: Among 1,402 PE-positive examinations, overall sensitivity was 64.1% and specificity 98.8%; sensitivity was 68.7% versus 55.7% at the two highest-volume sites.
watch_item: Retrospective, report-based evaluation cannot establish whether temporal changes arose from data drift, undocumented threshold changes, or other factors.
paper_title: Silent Drift and Site-level Variance in Clinical AI: Real-world performance and subgroup analysis for post-market monitoring of an FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool for high-risk use case of pulmonary embolism
